findings.text: Device and CPU lookup operations return the energy domain currently attached to the given device or processor, yielding absence when the input handle is invalid or no domain was installed.

Registration operations create a performance domain for a device from a state count, driver callback bundle, CPU set and unit selector, failing when inputs are missing or a domain already exists, with the CPU variant also requesting a capacity review.
Unregistration detaches and frees a non CPU device domain and clears the device association, ignoring invalid handles and leaving CPU domains in place.

Update operations refresh domain data after system changes, including chip specific power refresh, frequency bound narrowing to exactly matching states, per CPU capacity alignment and deferred scheduler domain rebuild.
Hibernation query operations report whether the configured mode requests suspend, whether a hibernation transition is underway, and whether entry into platform hibernation is active.

Platform operations installer replaces the hibernation backend, requiring a complete callback set when present and adjusting the selected mode between platform and shutdown defaults under sleep exclusion.
Quiet execution helper runs a caller supplied function inside a full hibernation style freeze and device suspend envelope, returning the inner result or the failure encountered during preparation.
A usable performance table has strictly ordered frequencies, power values that are nonzero and bounded, and one entry per declared state produced through driver callbacks.

A successfully created CPU domain carries a unique identifier, a stored processor span within a fixed ceiling, and mutual linkage between domain, parent device and member processors; failure during table setup discards the domain and identifier.

Registration rejects missing inputs, duplicate device domains, missing CPU masks, overlapping CPU membership and mixed processor capacities within one domain, and requires microwatt units unless an artificial cost provider is present.
Frequency bound updates only succeed when both requested frequencies exactly match existing table entries and the lower bound does not exceed the upper; otherwise current limits remain unchanged.
Chip binning refresh preserves stored frequencies while recomputing power for each state, aborting the whole update when any recomputation fails.

Capacity alignment compares stored peak performance against current processor scaling, skips artificial domains and uninitialized processors, refreshes only mismatched domains from a duplicated table, and defers a retry when processor policy lookup fails.
Hibernation defaults to shutdown behaviour, switches to platform behaviour only while platform operations are installed, and exposes only the modes valid for current build and backend configuration.

Resume configuration accepts device path, numeric major minor forms and encoded device values, records the parsed target under sleep exclusion, clears any no resume request, and immediately attempts restoration.

Hibernation configuration storage includes toggles for compression use, resume suppression and hibernation suppression, resume waiting and delay controls, a fixed size resume path buffer, device and offset holders, a non saved suspend indicator and compressor name buffers.

Runtime hibernation state comprises a bounded mode enumeration with first and last helpers, active compressor name, backend pointer, atomic exclusivity counter, platform entry flag, freezer test flag and a test delay control.

Domain registration, unregistration and limit changes serialize on a dedicated domain mutex that also guards table pointer publication, while global list membership uses a separate list mutex and steady state table reads use read side critical sections.

Hibernation mode, backend pointer and resume target updates hold system sleep exclusion, software restoration additionally holds the global transition mutex, and quiet execution combines sleep exclusion with an exclusive hibernation acquisition.

Observed domain state comprises a state count, numeric identifier, flags, lower and upper usable indexes, list linkage, a replaceable table pointer and, for processor domains, an embedded processor span; each state carries power, frequency and a derived performance measure.

A valid platform backend provides the full lifecycle set covering begin and end, snapshot preparation and completion, low level entry, and restore preparation, cleanup and exit; incomplete sets are rejected.

Domain lifecycle progresses from absent through guarded creation, efficiency initialization and debug registration to globally listed and announced, with creation failures unwinding identifier, table and domain allocations.
Capacity maintenance scans each processor once per domain, refreshes mismatched non artificial domains, and reschedules itself after a delay when some processors lack policy information.

Quiet execution moves through console preparation, notification, filesystem freeze, process and thread freeze, device preparation and suspension, callback invocation, then symmetric resume, thaw and notification on both success and failure paths.

Software restoration validates the resume partition, checks image presence and compressor support, acquires exclusivity, freezes activity, loads the image, then always thaws and notifies before releasing resources.

Hibernation mode selection cycles among disabled, platform, shutdown, reboot, suspend where built, and test resume, with platform availability following backend installation and user writes validated against known labels.
Power sysfs entries expose hibernation mode selection, resume device identity and resume offset, supporting readback of current values and validated writes that reconfigure the subsystem.

Boot time resume probing honors no resume requests and availability checks before locating the partition and attempting restoration, while capacity review and scheduler rebuild execute deferred in workqueue context.

Energy handling reports invalid configuration for driver callback errors, unordered frequencies, out of range power, oversized CPU sets, capacity mismatch and missing exact frequency matches, plus exists conflicts and allocation exhaustion.

Hibernation paths fail safely on incomplete backends, busy prior transitions, missing resume partitions, unavailable decompression support, image absence and notification or freeze errors, unwinding freezes and consoles before returning status.
Standard hibernation image compressor identifier is lzo and alternate identifier is lz4, chosen from image header flags at resume.
User visible hibernation mode labels are platform shutdown reboot suspend when built and test resume, with disabled shown when hibernation is unavailable.
Resume device attribute presents major and minor numbers in colon separated decimal form, and resume offset presents a decimal block number.

Hibernation logging uses a dedicated subsystem prefix, test delay defaults to a small second count, resume path storage reserves a fixed length buffer, and compressor name storage follows the crypto maximum algorithm name length.
